clue.text: Angry people drink it in pubs

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the traditional British hoppy draught beer

explanation.surface: Cross customers knocking back drinks at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is the name of a classic British draught ale served in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means resentful as an adjective and names a well-hopped British ale as a noun.

clue.text: Meaning it is a short illness?

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so the phrase must lose that letter

parts.note: the three words run together as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what some phrase means as a quick description of a sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: Run 'Meaning it is' together and drop one A: MENINGITIS. The question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Meningitis is a serious disease, an inflammation of the membranes around brain and spinal cord.

clue.text: Try to get brown buns — hate being different

indicators.note: letters that are different from how they started have been rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone baking bread rolls is told to brown them but hates the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown buns' reads like baking advice, but the browning is of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying out in sunshine is how people seek a tan, so it is an attempt at turning bronzed.

clue.text: Pale friend takes cover

explanation.surface: A white-faced companion ducks for shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallid is a direct synonym of wan, describing a face lacking healthy colour.

clue.text: Sweat like salesman climbing pointed part of steeple

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading upward, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
the tapering top of a church tower

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman scaling a church steeple works up quite a sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: To perspire is the formal verb for producing moisture through skin pores, i.e. to sweat.

clue.text: One stands in the street, light-headed

definitions.text: One stands in the street, light-headed

parts.words: One stands in the street, light-headed
parts.note: surface reading: a dizzy person standing about outdoors
setter's reading: a street fixture with a lamp literally at its head

explanation.walkthrough: Light-headed usually means faint or giddy; here it means having a light on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall roadside pole carrying an electric lamp stands on every street with its bulb at the top.

clue.text: Odd clue pair worked out

indicators.note: something worked out has been reprocessed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver remarks that a couple of crossword clues, once solved, turned out strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar and odd are synonyms, both describing something strange or unusual.

clue.text: In north Scotland opening hotels

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: the initial letter of the country

explanation.surface: New hotels are opening in the far north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are small hotels or pubs offering lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Got up to see her

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of rise, stood or climbed up
second meaning: a girl's name, so a possible 'her'

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to go and greet a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' stands for any woman, so a female first name can define it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, and it is also a common woman's first name.

clue.text: Supremo tends to be a bit aloof

indicators.note: only a bit of the preceding words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: The boss is said to keep somewhat distant from staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote and aloof both describe someone emotionally distant and unapproachable.

clue.text: Disperses a group in Diss

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written; Diss is a market town in Norfolk
a band is a group, especially of musicians

explanation.surface: A musical group in a small English town breaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England, and is used whole here.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbands means breaks up an organisation and sends its members away, so it disperses them.

clue.text: Which helps keep your correspondence down?

definitions.text: Which helps keep your correspondence down?

parts.words: Which helps keep your correspondence down?
parts.note: surface reading: something that reduces how many letters you write
setter's reading: an object that physically holds letters flat on a desk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep down' suggests limiting the amount of mail; it means stopping papers blowing away.
explanation.definitionFit: This heavy desk ornament rests on loose sheets and letters to stop them drifting off.

clue.text: Sees Witney's upset — he saw what happened

indicators.note: something upset has been knocked over and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; Witney is an Oxfordshire town

explanation.surface: Someone notices the town of Witney is distressed and witnessed the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', so read 'Sees Witney is upset'. Witney is a small town in Oxfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyewitness is a person who personally observed an event, such as a crime or accident.

clue.text: Forbid it before one becomes a singer

explanation.surface: Someone is warned not to let a person turn into a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male vocalist whose voice lies between tenor and bass.

clue.text: With which one should see one's dentist?

definitions.text: With which one should see one's dentist?

parts.words: With which one should see one's dentist?
parts.note: surface reading: what one ought to bring along to a dental appointment
setter's reading: dentition named after organs of sight

explanation.walkthrough: The clue jokes that teeth named after eyes ought to be able to look at things.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the canine teeth of the upper jaw, sitting directly below the eyes.

clue.text: Interval is especially short during ceremony

indicators.note: happening during something means falling within its span, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: esp. is the standard short form of especially

explanation.surface: Someone notes the break in a ritual is notably brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a brief interval of relief or rest from something difficult.

clue.text: Being silly about smell is cruel

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Someone argues that being frivolous about body odour is unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM as a smell is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane means lacking compassion and causing suffering, a close synonym for heartless or brutal.

clue.text: They must take the blame for this treatment

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one word encloses another

parts.note: taking the rap means accepting the blame

explanation.surface: Others are told to accept responsibility for the care that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the rap' is an idiom for taking the blame, so RAP stands for the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is a course of healing care for a physical or mental disorder.

clue.text: It's one's job to change people's locks

definitions.text: It's one's job to change people's locks

parts.words: It's one's job to change people's locks
parts.note: surface reading: a locksmith who replaces door locks
setter's reading: locks of hair, which a salon worker restyles

explanation.walkthrough: Changing locks points to a locksmith; locks here are tresses on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional cuts and styles clients' tresses, transforming how their head of curls looks.

clue.text: He won't say no when moved, men say

indicators.note: letters that are moved shift position into a new arrangement

parts.note: the last two words taken as written

explanation.surface: Men claim a person never refuses once he is emotionally touched.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man is a sycophant who always agrees with superiors and never refuses them.

clue.text: Blackleg takes second taxi

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker grabs another taxi to cross the picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackleg is British slang for a worker who breaks a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Scab is the insulting term for a worker who keeps working during an industrial strike.

clue.text: Don't eat quickly

explanation.surface: A warning against bolting food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food deliberately, and as an adverb it means rapidly.

clue.text: Mail once distributed by fuel supplier

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Post was formerly delivered by the company selling heating fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is the pit where coal, a fuel, is dug out and supplied.

clue.text: … or embraced by a girl on the beach?

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held within its arms, so it goes inside

explanation.surface: A seaside scene where someone is hugged by a young woman on the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots only tie the surface to the previous clue; they carry no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land beside the water rather than at sea, which is where the beach is.

clue.text: Body odour badly taints plant specialist

parts.note: BO is the standard abbreviation for body odour

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A smelly scientist spoils the greenhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanist is a scientist who studies plant life and its biology.

clue.text: He removes her tag

indicators.note: removes can be read as re-moves, moving the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: A man takes off a woman's label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is any male, so a man's first name can define it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gareth is a Welsh masculine first name, so it names a possible male person.
